Ravi S.: heads-up: found a weird resume token collision in the sampleapp when a client opens two parallel streams (multiplexing). can repro locally.
Hannah W.: describe the collision?
Ravi S.: steps: 1) start sampleapp that opens stream A and B concurrently 2) simulate a quick drop on A only 3) reconnect A with resume token 'sess-7' 4) server sometimes replays buffered fragments from B into A or vice-versa. feels like resume token namespace leak.
Olivia K.: are tokens scoped per connection? which SDKs are implicated?
Ravi S.: node SDK issues a user-scoped resume key by default (e.g., `resume:user:123:sess-7`) while python SDK in sampleapp was using `resume:sess-7` (no user/conn id). when two streams reuse the same sess-7 id (happens in demo harness), resume lookup is ambiguous and router picks the first buffer it finds.
Marco P.: ouch. so not strictly SSE framing, more metadata / token namespacing bug. can you paste minimal logs?
Ravi S.: paste:
```
# stream A reconnect
> GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1
> Host: staging.api
> Last-Event-ID: sess-7
> X-Client-Conn: c-A
# router resume lookup used key "resume:sess-7" -> returned buffer for c-B
# result: A received fragments belonging to B
```
Hannah W.: that explains the interleaving. sampleapp's harness reuses short ids for ease, but production sdks include connection-id. parity bug between sdks and sampleapp.
Olivia K.: quick fixes: 1) server-side: make resume storage keyed by (client-id or connection-id) + token; fallback to global only with a strict trust check. 2) router should verify an additional header (e.g., `X-Client-Conn`) or authentication fingerprint before applying a resumed buffer. 3) sdks/sampleapps: ensure resume tokens are namespaced by connection-id or use long random uuids per stream.
Marco P.: + add an e2e: spawn two streams from same sampleapp, give them the same short token, drop one, reconnect, assert no cross-delivery. Would catch regressions.
Ravi S.: created draft PRs: sampleapp/#77 (namespace resume tokens by conn-id + use uuid), platform/router/#421 (strict resume-keying + fingerprint check). CI kicked.
ci-bot: build 12134 started for sampleapp/#77.
Hannah W.: also add a compatibility shim for older sdks: if server sees an unscoped token but auth indicates same user has multiple active connections, refuse resume and ask client to re-open (fail-safe), plus a clear error so integrators can upgrade.
Olivia K.: docs: add a small note in SDK onboarding about resume token scoping and a recommended pattern: `resume:{user_id}:{conn_id}:{uuid}`. sampleapp demo should switch to that so new users don't hit this while learning.
Marco P.: will add unit tests for resume-store to ensure collisions cause a safe reject rather than silent cross-delivery. also add logging that surfaces when a token is matched but the connection-id doesn't match.
Ravi S.: thanks — will follow up with a short blurb in the release notes and a tiny FAQ in devex about multiplexing pitfalls ("Why did I get someone else's fragments?").
Hannah W.: nice find. can we also add a lint in sampleapp tests that fails if resume token generation is shorter than 16 chars? prevents accidental reuse in demos.
Ravi S.: good call, adding that to PR.
ci-bot: build 12134 passed for sampleapp/#77 (flaky tests skipped).
Olivia K.: follow-ups: 1) roll router change behind feature flag 2) monitor errors for a week after rollout 3) update SDK changelogs.
Marco P.: i'll own the router roll and e2e. thanks team.
